translations.reason: Standard tblastn protein neighborhood lookup construction and scanning
translations.validation: Focused standalone original-C/Rust complete-output comparison over 16 constructed tables (four protein query patterns, thresholds 0/13, normal/small bones): metadata, every occupied cell, PV and full overflow arrays; all scan hits and restart states with 0/1/minimum/roomy capacities and one/two subject ranges. Original constructors/neighbor enumeration/finalizers/scanners execute unchanged. Normal/small cell sizes checked as 16/12 bytes. Temporary /tmp/btyper-aa-lookup-* harnesses only; no broad fixture corpus added. Safe-hoist follow-up: unchanged pinned-C16-table comparison rerun in debug and optimized Rust; all2735 output lines (metadata/cells/PV/overflow and complete scan hit/restart streams, including capacity0/1/longest/roomy and one/two ranges) match exactly. Standalone equivalent compiler inspection reduces small-scanner bounds-panic sites8to4 and stack216to200bytes; this is code-generation evidence, not a speed claim. Broad whole-search raw parity and paired timing are coordinated by parent on the combined frozen artifact.
translations.adaptations: Scoped to ordinary non-PSSM amino-acid lookup used by standard tblastn. Preserve table geometry, query offset/hit ordering, threshold comparisons and original loop/branch order. Borrowed slices and owned Vecs replace C sequence blocks, pointer/count arrays and allocation/free; ordinary Rust allocation failure behavior applies. PSSM, RPS and compressed protein lookup paths are excluded. Typed AminoAcidSubject provides original sequence and half-open sequence ranges. Preserve full three-element scanning state, priming/incremental indexes, PV lookup, inline/overflow selection, all-or-nothing word-list copying and restart offset on insufficient capacity. Profile-guided safe representation hoist: borrow local PV/backbone/overflow slices; validate the complete declared output capacity and each scannable subject span once; iterate the incoming residue bytes directly with unchanged rolling-index arithmetic and source position progression. Validate each complete source/destination hit run once, then zip source entries with destination elements instead of indexing each output hit. Small inline u16 entries are decoded from native-endian two-byte chunks in the same union byte order. No unchecked/unsafe indexing, table/cell layout change, masking, hit-order change, capacity/restart change or algorithm replacement. Original ComputeTableIndexIncremental function remains available; scan loop expands its identical last-character arithmetic to avoid constructing a suffix slice per position.

integration: Only src/core/blast_aascan.rs changes; no lookup/cell geometry or shared API changes. Source function mapping/ranges/hashes remain unchanged.
Frozen implementation is the simple safe span/hit-run view hoist only. Padded PV/const specialization trial stayed under /tmp and was not adopted; no extra copy or stackPV exists in production.

Source mask32767 exceeds 28-letter backbone maximum28539, so mask alone is not a valid proof for table bounds. Production retains safe PV/backbone guards. A further one-time-PV-coverage plus pre-PV index guard experiment stayed under /tmp; it retained per-position checks and increased stack, so it was not adopted.
Pending whole-search regression and benchmark coordination uses combined AA/NucScratch/masked-identity source freeze. No speed improvement claimed from compilation or isolated scanner equivalence.
